claims.text: Texas Children's Hospital dated its release on the BRSK1 study September 28th, 2026, with a Houston dateline.
claims.quote: HOUSTON (September 28, 2026)
claims.document: Texas Children's Hospital news release, September 28th, 2026

claims.text: Researchers at the Duncan Neurological Research Institute at Texas Children's Hospital, Baylor College of Medicine and the Texome Project, with collaborating institutions, report the BRSK1 finding.
claims.quote: Researchers at the Duncan Neurological Research Institute (Duncan NRI) at Texas Children's Hospital, Baylor College of Medicine, the Texome Project and collaborating institutions
claims.document: Texas Children's Hospital news release, September 28th, 2026

claims.text: The team identified variants in the gene BRSK1 as a likely diagnosis for a rare, complex neurodevelopmental disorder that had gone unexplained for the people who have it.
claims.quote: have identified variants in gene BRSK1 as a likely diagnosis for individuals with a rare and complex neurodevelopmental disorder who until now had not received an explanation for their condition
claims.document: Texas Children's Hospital news release, September 28th, 2026

claims.text: The study is published in the American Journal of Human Genetics.
claims.quote: The study appears in the American Journal of Human Genetics
claims.document: Texas Children's Hospital news release, September 28th, 2026

claims.text: The work started with one child enrolled in the Texome Project, which the Texas Children's release describes as free genetic testing for medically underserved people with rare, undiagnosed conditions.
claims.quote: The project began with a child enrolled in the Texome Project, a program that provides free genetic testing for medically underserved individuals with rare, undiagnosed conditions
claims.document: Texas Children's Hospital news release, September 28th, 2026

claims.text: Hugo Bellen is a Distinguished Service Professor in Baylor's Department of Molecular and Human Genetics and chair in neurogenetics at the Duncan NRI, and a co-lead author of the study.
claims.quote: co-lead author Dr. Hugo Bellen, Distinguished Service Professor in the Department of Molecular and Human Genetics at Baylor and chair in neurogenetics at the Duncan NRI
claims.document: Texas Children's Hospital news release, September 28th, 2026

claims.text: Standard genetic analyses of a parent and child with the condition found no answer.
claims.quote: Standard genetic analyses of a parent and child with the condition did not reveal an answer
claims.document: Texas Children's Hospital news release, September 28th, 2026

claims.text: An AI tool called AI-MARRVEL then analyzed the genomic data and flagged a rare change in BRSK1 as a promising candidate diagnosis.
claims.quote: when a new artificial intelligence-based tool called AI-MARRVEL analyzed the genomic data, it highlighted a rare change in the BRSK1 gene as a promising candidate for a genetic diagnosis
claims.document: Texas Children's Hospital news release, September 28th, 2026

claims.text: The researchers shared the finding through the GeneMatcher network, and other families reported rare variants in the same gene.
claims.quote: After sharing this finding through a research network called GeneMatcher, additional families reported rare variants in the same gene
claims.document: Texas Children's Hospital news release, September 28th, 2026

claims.text: The study covered 10 affected people from seven unrelated families, according to first author Mingxi Deng, a postdoctoral fellow in the Bellen lab.
claims.quote: Altogether, we studied 10 affected individuals from seven unrelated families
claims.document: Texas Children's Hospital news release, September 28th, 2026

claims.text: Every affected person had some developmental delay, though how severe it was and which symptoms appeared differed from person to person.
claims.quote: All affected individuals showed some degree of developmental delay, but the severity and specific symptoms varied
claims.document: Texas Children's Hospital news release, September 28th, 2026

claims.text: Common features were delayed speech and language, intellectual disability, autism, ADHD, anxiety, low muscle tone and a smaller than average head.
claims.quote: Common features included delayed speech and language development, intellectual disability, autism spectrum disorder, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, anxiety, low muscle tone and microcephaly
claims.document: Texas Children's Hospital news release, September 28th, 2026

claims.text: Two of the affected people had seizures.
claims.quote: Two individuals experienced seizures.
claims.document: Texas Children's Hospital news release, September 28th, 2026

claims.text: Relatives who carried the same variant had symptoms anywhere from mild to severe, which the researchers call variable expressivity.
claims.quote: Even among members of the same family carrying the same genetic variant, symptoms ranged from mild to severe.
claims.document: Texas Children's Hospital news release, September 28th, 2026

claims.text: To test whether the variants disrupt the gene, the team used the lab fruit fly, which shares many biological pathways with humans.
claims.quote: Fruit flies share many biological pathways with humans
claims.document: Texas Children's Hospital news release, September 28th, 2026

claims.text: The fly version of BRSK1 is called sff, short for sugar-free frosting, and it is active mostly in neurons, as in humans.
claims.quote: We studied the fly equivalent of BRSK1, called sff (sugar-free frosting), and found that this gene is active primarily in neurons
claims.document: Texas Children's Hospital news release, September 28th, 2026

claims.text: Flies with the gene switched off had trouble moving, were more prone to seizure-like behavior and heat-induced paralysis, and died younger.
claims.quote: When the fly gene was disabled, the flies developed difficulties moving, showed increased sensitivity to stressors that can trigger seizure-like behavior, became more vulnerable to heat-induced paralysis and lived shorter lives
claims.document: Texas Children's Hospital news release, September 28th, 2026

claims.text: Adding the normal human BRSK1 gene to flies lacking sff largely fixed their movement and neurological problems, showing the two genes do similar jobs.
claims.quote: the human gene largely corrected the flies' movement and neurological problems
claims.document: Texas Children's Hospital news release, September 28th, 2026

claims.text: The patients' versions of the gene restored the flies only partly, which suggests the variants weaken the protein without wiping out its activity.
claims.quote: the neurological and movement problems were only partially restored, suggesting that these variants reduce but do not completely eliminate the protein's activity
claims.document: Texas Children's Hospital news release, September 28th, 2026

claims.text: Losing BRSK1 activity raised levels of a protein that organizes microtubules, the internal scaffolding of neurons.
claims.quote: increased levels of a protein involved in organizing microtubules, a structural framework inside neurons
claims.document: Texas Children's Hospital news release, September 28th, 2026

claims.text: Deng notes that microtubule disruption has been tied to several neurodevelopmental and neurological disorders.
claims.quote: Microtubule disruption has been linked to several neurodevelopmental and neurological disorders
claims.document: Texas Children's Hospital news release, September 28th, 2026

claims.text: The release concludes the patient variants cause a disorder of developmental delay plus neurological and behavioral symptoms, with or without epilepsy.
claims.quote: a disorder characterized by developmental delays and a range of neurological and behavioral symptoms, with or without epilepsy
claims.document: Texas Children's Hospital news release, September 28th, 2026

claims.text: Bellen credits the result to pairing AI-driven gene discovery with experiments in model organisms.
claims.quote: highlights the power of combining AI-driven gene discovery with experimental studies in model organisms
claims.document: Texas Children's Hospital news release, September 28th, 2026

claims.text: Co-lead author Michael Wangler, an associate professor at Baylor and a Duncan NRI investigator, says the team wanted to build a program focused on families in Texas.
claims.quote: we wanted to build a program focused on families in Texas
claims.document: Texas Children's Hospital news release, September 28th, 2026

claims.text: Wangler says the project learned along the way how AI can help interpret genomic data.
claims.quote: As the project progressed, we learned how artificial intelligence can help us interpret genomic data.
claims.document: Texas Children's Hospital news release, September 28th, 2026

claims.text: The peer-reviewed paper is titled Monoallelic variants in BRSK1 are associated with a neurodevelopmental disorder with or without epilepsy.
claims.quote: Monoallelic variants in BRSK1 are associated with a neurodevelopmental disorder with or without epilepsy
claims.document: Deng et al., American Journal of Human Genetics, DOI 10.1016/j.ajhg.2026.09.005, abstract via Europe PMC

claims.text: The paper itself says the first patient was found in the Texome Project using AI-MARRVEL, and describes Texome as serving financially disadvantaged people in Texas.
claims.quote: An individual with a variant in BRSK1 was identified in the Texome Project, which provides genomic diagnosis to financially disadvantaged individuals in Texas, using AI-MARRVEL
claims.document: Deng et al., American Journal of Human Genetics, DOI 10.1016/j.ajhg.2026.09.005, abstract via Europe PMC

claims.text: The paper says nine more people carrying rare BRSK1 variants were found through GeneMatcher.
claims.quote: We subsequently found nine individuals harboring rare heterozygous BRSK1 variants through GeneMatcher
claims.document: Deng et al., American Journal of Human Genetics, DOI 10.1016/j.ajhg.2026.09.005, abstract via Europe PMC

claims.text: The team modeled three of the patients' missense variants in fruit flies.
claims.quote: We utilized Drosophila to model three missense variants
claims.document: Deng et al., American Journal of Human Genetics, DOI 10.1016/j.ajhg.2026.09.005, abstract via Europe PMC

claims.text: The paper names the raised protein as Futsch, the fly counterpart of MAP1B, which binds microtubules.
claims.quote: elevated levels of Futsch (MAP1B), a microtubule-associated protein
claims.document: Deng et al., American Journal of Human Genetics, DOI 10.1016/j.ajhg.2026.09.005, abstract via Europe PMC

claims.text: The authors conclude that losing one working copy of BRSK1 leads to a neurodevelopmental syndrome whose features vary.
claims.quote: heterozygous loss of BRSK1 leads to a neurodevelopmental syndrome with variable phenotypes
claims.document: Deng et al., American Journal of Human Genetics, DOI 10.1016/j.ajhg.2026.09.005, abstract via Europe PMC

claims.text: AI-MARRVEL was described in a peer-reviewed paper in NEJM AI.
claims.quote: AI-MARRVEL - A Knowledge-Driven AI System for Diagnosing Mendelian Disorders
claims.document: Mao et al., NEJM AI, DOI 10.1056/aioa2300009, abstract via Europe PMC

claims.text: AI-MARRVEL is a random forest machine learning classifier trained on more than 3.5 million variants from thousands of diagnosed cases.
claims.quote: uses a random-forest machine-learning classifier trained on over 3.5 million variants from thousands of diagnosed cases
claims.document: Mao et al., NEJM AI, DOI 10.1056/aioa2300009, abstract via Europe PMC

claims.text: Across three real-world patient groups, AI-MARRVEL doubled the number of solved cases compared with the methods it was benchmarked against.
claims.quote: doubling the number of solved cases as compared with benchmarked methods, across three distinct real-world cohorts
claims.document: Mao et al., NEJM AI, DOI 10.1056/aioa2300009, abstract via Europe PMC

claims.text: On a confidence metric built to pick diagnosable cases out of unsolved ones, AI-MARRVEL reached 98% precision and found 57% of diagnosable cases among 871 cases. That figure is not an overall diagnostic accuracy.
claims.quote: we designed a confidence metric on which AIM achieved a precision rate of 98% and identified 57% of diagnosable cases out of a collection of 871 cases
claims.document: Mao et al., NEJM AI, DOI 10.1056/aioa2300009, abstract via Europe PMC

claims.text: An online version of AI-MARRVEL is available at ai.marrvel.org.
claims.quote: The online version of AIM is available at https://ai.marrvel.org
claims.document: Mao et al., NEJM AI, DOI 10.1056/aioa2300009, abstract via Europe PMC

claims.text: GeneMatcher is a tool that connects people interested in the same gene.
claims.quote: GeneMatcher (genematcher.org) is a tool designed to connect individuals with an interest in the same gene.
claims.document: Hamosh et al., Human Mutation, PMID 35170833, abstract via Europe PMC

claims.text: The Texome Project states its mission as making expert genetic services reachable for people with no insurance or no way to pay for genomic testing.
claims.quote: making genetic services from leading experts in the field more accessible to participants who have no insurance or are unable to pay for genomic testing
claims.document: The Texome Project home page

claims.text: Texome lists as candidates people from underserved populations with a suspected rare disease who can't pay for DNA sequencing.
claims.quote: Individuals from an underserved population with a suspected rare disease and without the means to pay for DNA sequencing
claims.document: The Texome Project, For Patients

claims.text: Texome says its genetic testing and follow-up consultations are free.
claims.quote: The genetic testing and following consultations will come at no cost.
claims.document: The Texome Project, For Patients

claims.text: Participants receive a $100 gift card after all 5 visits.
claims.quote: At the end of all 5 visits, you will receive a $100 gift card
claims.document: The Texome Project, For Patients

claims.text: A family that thinks it may qualify can contact the Texome Project by email at texome-project@bcm.edu.
claims.quote: If you think you could be eligible or have questions please don't hesitate to contact us at texome-project@bcm.edu
claims.document: The Texome Project, For Patients

claims.text: The Texome study runs 5 visits over 2 years, in person or virtual.
claims.quote: The study consists of 5 visits (in-person or virtual) over a 2 year period
claims.document: The Texome Project, About

claims.text: Texome is funded by the National Human Genome Research Institute.
claims.quote: We receive funding from National Human Genome Research Institute (1R01HG011795-01).
claims.document: The Texome Project, About

claims.text: The name Texome joins Texas and exome, the type of genetic analysis the study provides.
claims.quote: Our name comes from a combination of the words Texas and exome.
claims.document: The Texome Project, About

claims.text: Texome states a plan to sequence roughly 400 children with undiagnosed disorders, with their parents. That is a target, not a count of families served.
claims.quote: We will perform trio whole exome sequencing for diagnostic purposes in ~400 children with undiagnosed disorders.
claims.document: The Texome Project, For Providers

claims.text: Texome focuses on Texas but accepts applications from other states.
claims.quote: Though we are focused on populations in Texas, we are open to applications from other states as well.
claims.document: The Texome Project, For Providers

claims.text: Texome says many people in the Houston area lack access to genomic medicine because it costs too much and insurance does not cover it.
claims.quote: many individuals in the Houston area are largely underserved and lack access to genomic medicine because of prohibitive cost and lack of insurance coverage
claims.document: The Texome Project, For Providers

claims.text: Texome describes the tool it uses on exome data as using AI to find disease links people miss.
claims.quote: This tool is integrated with artificial intelligence to sift through all the data and identify disease relationships that humans can't always connect.
claims.document: The Texome Project, For Patients

claims.text: Texome follows participants with re-evaluation at 6 months, 1 year and 2 years.
claims.quote: at 6 months, 1 year and 2 years in which we will re-evaluate key genes in the context of the individual
claims.document: The Texome Project, For Patients

claims.text: In the fly test, all three patient-derived variants provided only a partial rescue.
claims.quote: the three individual-derived alleles (BRSK1<sup>p.Ile202Val</sup>, BRSK1<sup>p.Arg237Cys</sup>, and BRSK1<sup>p.Thr406Ile</sup>) provide only a partial rescue
claims.document: Deng et al., American Journal of Human Genetics, DOI 10.1016/j.ajhg.2026.09.005, abstract via Europe PMC
